newsitem.title: DENMARK: FDA to speed up diabetes drug review-Novo.
newsitem.headline: FDA to speed up diabetes drug review-Novo.

text.p: Danish biotechnological group Novo Nordisk said on Monday that the U.S. Food & Drug Administration (FDA) had put its new oral anti-diabetes-two agent repaglinide on a shorter six-month review schedule.

It said the FDA's normal approval time for such drugs was 12-18 months but added that the reclassification was not any assurance of a decision within the shorter time frame nor a guarantee for its approval of repaglinide.

"With our focus on diabetes care as one of our core businesses, Novo Nordisk considers repaglinide a product of major strategic importance, offering people with type-2 diabetes a drug with therapeutic advantages over currently available oral anti-diabetic drugs," Novo said in a statement.
Repaglinide is the first of a new chemical class of orally administered drugs for the treatment of type-2 diabetes designed to regulate blood glucose during meal times, it said.

Novo Nordisk said it filed for regulatory approval of repaglinide, which was developed in cooperation with Germany's Boehringer Ingelheim GmbH, with the FDA and European Union authorities in June 1997.
